Does an intermediate m90 condition connect the measured 50 and 150 µl endpoints smoothly?
For m125, do lower-volume and loading-solvent-volume contrasts explain the large 2/1 tail shift while the 5/1 curve remains comparatively stable?
Does the weak-ratio end of the m167 curve continue its measured V2-dominant progression?
Does a lower-volume EA measurement for m92 extend the measured EA tail coherently?

possible_model_blind_spots: The model may conflate PE/EA ratio, density, injection volume, loading amount, loading-solvent volume, and loading solvent. Matched contrasts are more interpretable than isolated extreme predictions.
Positional isomers and superficially similar aza-aromatics can have different silica interactions and residual signs, as shown by the m160/m161 and m216/m211 records.
V1 and V2 errors may be correlated in the high-volume tail, but the observed residuals do not support one common offset. Endpoint-specific or joint residual structure may be needed.

Candidate volume, novelty, similarity, and quantile width are prediction diagnostics, not evidence that a true label will be extreme or erroneous.

ml_scientist.state_summary: Seed 157, free_llm32_dual_expert_v1, round 2: 397 observed records, 2,933 reported legal candidates, no pending experiments and no validation/test records. Measured feedback favors molecule-specific response shapes and condition-dependent loading effects. m167 now has substantial coverage; unresolved m125 contrasts and broader molecular transfer offer plausible higher marginal information. Candidate predictions remain diagnostics, and acquired feedback does not establish independent Row accuracy after retraining.
ml_scientist.important_observations:
H1 remains supported with refinement. At 150 µl, measured m167 V1/V2 progress from 4.392/12.433 at 2/1 (d1e6e925623ba4b6810b), through 4.983/20.142 at 20/1 (ddf2f769007f3d9f75fd), to 5.025/22.400 at 50/1 (fa6fd34875fdc7acf6c1). V2 remains more responsive, with a shallower high-ratio continuation. Across matched ratios 2/1, 5/1, 10/1 and 50/1, increasing load from 50 to 150 µl lowers V1 by approximately 1.13–1.21 ml. The corresponding V2 increase grows from about 0.13 to 2.39 ml. This supports a local ratio/loading interaction and weakens complete separability.

H2 gains local support but no universal direction. At m160 2/1, increasing load from 50 to 150 µl changes measured V1/V2 from 14.142/34.067 (b21061720e23b7a5bdcb) to 11.517/33.075 (36d971e3231c54486d05). At m90 5/1, the change is 37.800/67.900 (29db30571b2a1ae59cc7) to 27.475/65.408 (b51b5dbcd2a38b174973). These V2 directions differ from m167; experimental variability remains an alternative explanation for individual contrasts.

H5 remains a difficult local regime, but a pervasive large loading effect is weakened. At m125 5/1 with 300 µl solvent volume, 100 and 150 µl loads give similar measured endpoints: 42.958/73.100 (74cf50c6ec476a394b01) and 42.267/74.042 (549daca56bed1c9d2bcc). Its striking 2/1 contrast changes both load and solvent volume: 100/300 µl gives 15.408/29.583 (c8d43713db33bf820a1d), while 150/500 µl gives 32.950/69.808 (facbcedbecb46072b04c). Observed 69f9cefb952abd22672c is actually m101 at 20/1, so the additional m125 contrast described in memory was not completed.

H3 is supported as heterogeneous local error structure. m160 has small V2 premeasurement errors at 2/1 despite its earlier 52.81 ml underprediction at 5/1. m216 was overpredicted by 11.63/10.36 ml at 5/1 (33ffc69a253a89f15995), while its earlier 10/1 prediction missed by -27.69/-41.93 ml (e47aebe2660b9e1528de). New large underpredictions for m212 and m146 coexist with overprediction for m211. A universal polar or basic-nitrogen offset remains unsupported. These errors came from successive model versions.

H6 is retained within its measured scope: m147 remains a shallow-response counterexample. H4's historical m13/m80 reversal premise remains rejected because their measured endpoints and recorded premeasurement predictions are ordered.
ml_scientist.important_model_behaviors:
Current prediction diagnostic: predictions near newly measured tails move toward their labels. m160 at 5/1 and 50 µl predicts 40.756/98.255 ml, near the measured 100 µl result 40.583/98.392. m216 at 10/1 and 100 µl predicts 53.438/92.852, near the measured 50 µl result 53.417/92.933. This indicates local adjustment, not independent predictive improvement.

Current sensitivity diagnostic: loading responses are frequently almost flat. The missing m125 2/1 factorial corners predict approximately 23.1/47.5 ml despite different load/solvent-volume combinations and substantially different measured diagonal corners. Such low-sensitivity points can test competing systematic explanations even without high nominal uncertainty.

Quantile diagnostic: V1 q10 repeatedly equals zero, so its nominal width largely tracks endpoint scale. Quantiles also cross: 9c06d41471b0bc70e4c7 has V2 q10 10.223 above q90 10.102 and a negative width. Other medians exceed q90. These fields cannot support calibrated uncertainty ranking as supplied.

Separate from the rejected historical premise, current candidate 02ddeed8a16d3adf3e28 genuinely predicts crossed endpoints, 6.198/5.086 ml. This is an output-coherence diagnostic, not measured chromatography or sufficient justification for another ordering experiment.
ml_scientist.possible_learning_bottlenecks:
Inference: learning response shape between measured conditions may now matter more than repeating an already labeled high endpoint. Intermediate ratios around m125, m146, m212, m31 and m92 can distinguish slope transfer from a localized transition.

Measured historical evidence supports attention to V2: premeasurement misses were -32.64 ml for m92 at 50/1 (7b42519983cf93dd7efd), -32.70 ml for m212 at 10/1 (70cba7a21b5a01fb8e73), and -28.32 ml for m146 at 10/1 (9e3ce3497298084abd83). Conversely, m105 and m199 at 0/1 were overpredicted by 8.71 and 6.07 ml. Tail risk has both signs.

Observed identical-input variability limits interpretation. m174 records 704ba630f25fe7f20166 and 92bac523bed1042d6a75 share all recorded conditions but differ by about 4.68/5.93 ml. m105 records fa64656d7b055dec7f56 and a8a8b4ab0ef68c063c29 differ by about 2.08 ml on V2. Repetition can estimate variability conditional on recorded inputs; it cannot alone separate measurement noise from missing covariates.

ML priors: weak use of loading features is plausible, especially for V1, but representation, regularization and sparse contrasts remain competing causes. Joint endpoint learning could help correlated residuals while preserving endpoint-specific effects. Universal hard monotonicity is not established.
ml_scientist.coverage_or_redundancy_concerns:
Exact condition duplicates are common: c87f9f22f58a227ebe61 and 7a2f7cc9ffd95dd9cfa7 have identical m54 conditions and predictions. Assess marginal information using molecule identity and all five condition fields; retain duplicate multiplicity when considering the Row distribution. Some legal candidates also duplicate observed inputs, so new IDs do not necessarily add coverage.

The pool includes familiar low-volume halogenated/nonpolar and ester/carbonyl families, plus unmeasured molecules including m107, m37, m47, m117, m116, m129, m191, m205 and m206. Novelty is more useful with an interpretable family or condition comparison. The extensively measured m167, m105 and m147 grids need explicit unresolved questions to justify further labels.

Similarity-to-pending supplies no diversity information because pending is empty. Molecular similarity of 1 does not establish condition coverage or equivalence of loading response.
ml_scientist.warnings:
Use observed-table rows to resolve memory conflicts. Besides the m101/m125 mismatch for 69f9cefb952abd22672c, observed 96710afeabc594baa359 is m90 at 100 µl, not 150 µl. Stored rationales would otherwise misidentify loading contrasts.

PE/EA is the mobile-phase ratio; DCM, PE and EA in the loading-solvent field are separate variables. Memory references to PE/DCM ratio and several stronger/weaker-eluent descriptions are unreliable. Higher PE/EA is PE-richer under the stated encoding. Structure annotations also need correction: m199 is a sulfoxide and m174 is an ester.

Historical residuals are premeasurement errors from this trajectory, not current candidate errors. Adaptively acquired feedback and curated high-error examples cannot establish unbiased Row accuracy or retraining gains. V2−V1 is chromatographic endpoint separation, not predictive uncertainty.
